TITLE: 'Starmer sabotages Burnham' and 'Best of buddies'

SOURCE: BBC

DAILY TELEGRAPH (lead): "Starmer sabotages Burnham on Brexit"
- Starmer "has raised the prospect of rejoining the EU" while Burnham "seeks to keep Leave voters on side"
- Despite Burnham's "previous desire to reverse the 2016 referendum"

DAILY MIRROR (lead): "Starmer's defiant message: I won't walk away"
- Quotes Starmer "defiant"; "rejects call to set out departure timetable"
- Despite pressure from Labour MPs and senior ministers

FINANCIAL TIMES (lead): "Burnham tries to ease markets while vowing to reverse sell-off"
- Burnham's pledge to "reassure markets he will not rip up the UK's fiscal rules"
- Despite plans to "reverse privatisation and austerity"
- Attempted to reassure investors he would not embark on "irresponsible borrowing policies"

DAILY MAIL (lead): "Slippery Burnham's two u-turns in one day" (red banner "Labour's civil war")
- Re fiscal rules + Brexit remarks

THE TIMES (lead): "Burnham 'far ahead of Starmer' in Labour vote"
- YouGov polling: Burnham would win 59% of membership vote vs Starmer 37% in head-to-head
- Lammy floated lifting age of criminal responsibility from 10 to up to 14 in England/Wales
- Government also eyeing Scotland's law where children cannot be charged with criminal offences before age 12

GUARDIAN (lead): "Burnham: Labour must change to regain trust"
- Burnham would make his fight about "national issues where Labour was failing, in a direct challenge to the prime minister"

DAILY EXPRESS: "Britons want to keep pension triple lock" (66% back the guarantee)

i PAPER: "HS2 will cost more than NASA's Artemis Moon mission"
- Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander to release Tuesday review
- Costs set to reach ~£100bn — more than NASA's £79bn Artemis budget
